findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - A developer selects Me after their one-hour fix and a teammate's nine-hour fix merge today. The page shows the team-wide five-hour median beside only the developer's items. The previous median used the filtered `recent` rows, but this line always takes the unfiltered snapshot value. The Fixes and Story parts selections have the same inconsistency. The Me view is specified as filtered to the viewer's items in `plans/FORGE-BOARD-4.md:13`.
findings.title: Functional: Keep the daily median scoped to the Me view

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 2
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - A teammate fetches the default branch just after another machine merges an item, while the teammate's 60-second PR cache still lists it as open. `board.py:578-579` can identify the merge time from Git, but `board.py:638-640` passes only the missing PR merge time to the duration calculation. With no local `item finished` event, `time_records.py:172-176` leaves the duration unmeasured, so the daily median excludes the newly merged item or says there were no measured merges. The figure can therefore disagree across teammates despite both start and merge times being available.
findings.title: Functional: Use the known merge time when PR data is stale

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - A team lands several items, or an item spends longer waiting for CI than for the owner. The named proof exercises only single-item land and one dominant owner wait, so it would pass if batch land omitted a measurement or the cause were hard-coded to the owner. Its `merged \S+` assertion also accepts an arbitrary merge timestamp. Finally, `tests/test_last_task_records_story_outcome.py:22-24` supplies no PR body and the fixture retains local events, so the test does not establish that the output can use the shared How it went record.
findings.title: Gate: test_1_merge_and_land_print_start_to_merge_time

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - A fix and a story part both merge today, or an item merges today without a recorded start. This test calculates a median for two fixes, while test 1 checks a task only on its own; both would pass if tasks were excluded whenever fixes are present. The unmeasured assertion covers items moved to yesterday, not a merge today whose duration is unmeasured. Those cases are part of the named board proof and can produce a wrong daily figure while the current tests pass.
findings.title: Gate: test_2_board_shows_daily_median_from_merge_history

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 2
Raise: Gate
Case: normal use - The changed Now screen renders the daily figure. Its render-list entry still waives every cut-text finding because card titles supposedly use a one-line ellipsis (`tests/test_board_plan_stays_open.py:485-488`). That reason is obsolete: `src/forge/board_app/now.css:136-140` now wraps those titles. The waiver consequently suppresses clipping checks across the changed screen without a current reason.
findings.title: Gate: rendered check

why: The owner measures time from a task or fix start to its merge, but merge prints no such time and the board shows no daily figure, so it is read by hand from records
